cands.bio: Santa Clarita City Council member since 2020, representing District 3. He served as Mayor of Santa Clarita from 2022 to 2023. He ran as a Republican for California's 27th Congressional District in 2026 and lost to incumbent George Whitesides (D).

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California endorsed Gibbs in the 2026 race for California's 27th Congressional District. Ballotpedia also lists several online voter-guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Jason Gibbs was born or raised, or when he came to California. We also could not find his work history outside elected office, or his education. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, so we have no questionnaire answers from him. We found no documented statements or actions by him on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police funding, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. We also found no Santa Clarita City Council actions or votes by him on these topics. No documented controversies, foreign ties, or other endorsements turned up in the pages we had.

cands.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 27th District since January 2025. Former NASA Chief of Staff under President Obama and first CEO of Virgin Galactic. Co-founded Megafire Action, a wildfire-focused organization. Holds degrees from Princeton and the University of Cambridge.

endorsements.text: Los Angeles County Sheriff Robert Luna endorsed him for re-election on May 15, 2026.

2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.
2024 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include Sen. Mark Kelly, Sen. Alex Padilla, Rep. Nancy Pelosi, Gabrielle Giffords, the League of Conservation Voters and California Environmental Voters.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was raised or when he moved to California. We found no documented positions on data centers or on development, and no statements or actions on homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages we had. His campaign site describes bills he has introduced on tax relief for residents hit by environmental crises, firefighter health standards and pay, and housing for veterans, but it does not name them, so we left them out. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
